deck.title: Disaster Recovery
deck.analogy: DR strategies are kinds of spare tires: Backup & Restore is no spare (call a tow truck), Pilot Light is a donut in the trunk, Warm Standby is a full inflated spare, Active-Active is a second identical car driving alongside you.

subtopics.title: How to answer any DR question

cards.front: In disaster recovery, what does RPO (Recovery Point Objective) measure?

back.answer: Maximum acceptable data loss: how far back the tape rewinds.
back.explanation: Nightly backups mean an RPO of up to 24 hours of lost work.

cards.front: In disaster recovery, what does RTO (Recovery Time Objective) measure?

back.answer: Maximum acceptable downtime: how long until you are serving customers again.
back.explanation: RPO is time before the disaster (data lost); RTO is time after it (time down).

cards.front: How do the four DR strategies map to spare tires, and how does the exam choose between them?

back.answer: Backup & Restore = tow truck, Pilot Light = donut, Warm Standby = inflated spare, Active-Active = second car. Pick the cheapest that meets RPO/RTO.
back.explanation: Better spares cost more; same eliminate-then-cheapest logic as S3 storage classes.
back.mnemonic: Spare tires: none, donut, full spare, second car.

cards.front: DR Backup & Restore: what are its RTO, RPO, cost and DR-region footprint?

back.answer: RTO hours, RPO hours, cheapest ($); nothing runs in DR region, backups in S3, rebuild on disaster.
back.mnemonic: No spare, call a tow truck.

cards.front: DR Pilot Light: what are its RTO, RPO, cost and DR-region footprint?

back.answer: RTO tens of minutes, RPO minutes–seconds, $$; core only: DB continuously replicated, servers off/minimal.

cards.front: DR Warm Standby: what are its RTO, RPO, cost and DR-region footprint?

back.answer: RTO minutes, RPO seconds, $$$; scaled-down full copy always running, scale UP on disaster.

cards.front: DR Multi-Site Active-Active: what are its RTO, RPO, cost and DR-region footprint?

back.answer: RTO ~zero, RPO ~zero, $$$$; full capacity in both regions serving live traffic.
back.mnemonic: A second identical car driving alongside you.

cards.front: Keyword: **"Minimal DR footprint, database continuously replicated, compute launched only on disaster"**

back.explanation: The pilot flame is lit; the furnace is off.

cards.front: Keyword: **"A smaller version of the full environment is always running"**
Keyword: **"Zero downtime, both regions active"**
Keyword: **"Lowest cost, RTO of hours is fine"**
DR question says RTO is "a few hours". Why is Multi-Site Active-Active a wrong answer?

back.answer: It's better than needed but fails the cost qualifier; don't buy a better spare tire than asked.
back.explanation: Choose the cheapest strategy that meets the stated RPO/RTO.
back.mnemonic: Don't buy a better spare tire than asked.

cards.front: What RPO and RTO does Aurora Global Database provide for cross-region DR?

back.answer: RPO ~1 second, RTO under 1 minute, via cross-region replication.

cards.front: What role do DynamoDB Global Tables play in DR?

back.answer: Multi-region, multi-active NoSQL: writes can go to any region.

cards.front: What role does S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) play in DR?

back.answer: Copies objects to a bucket in another region.

cards.front: What does AWS Backup provide, and what is Vault Lock for?

back.answer: Centralized cross-service backup plans (EBS, RDS, DynamoDB, EFS…); Vault Lock makes backups immutable.

cards.front: What does AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (DRS) do?

back.answer: Continuous block-level replication of servers (on-prem or EC2) into AWS; RPO seconds, RTO minutes.

cards.front: How does Route 53 failover routing support DR?

back.answer: When a health check fails, DNS flips traffic to the DR region.

cards.front: Besides migration, what DR-related capability does AWS DMS offer?
What are the three steps for answering any DR exam question?

back.answer: Find stated RPO/RTO, eliminate strategies that can't meet them, pick the cheapest survivor.

cards.sourceHeading: How to answer any DR question

cards.front: DR needs RTO of 10 minutes and RPO of seconds, with reasonable costs. Which strategy?

back.explanation: Active-Active also works but costs more; Pilot Light is too slow.

choices.why: Meets minutes/seconds at lower cost than Active-Active.
Works but costs more than needed.

cards.front: DR is needed at the LOWEST cost and hours of downtime are acceptable. Which strategy?

back.explanation: Cheapest strategy that meets a relaxed RTO.

choices.why: Cheapest; hours of RTO are acceptable.

cards.front: An application must survive a region failure with zero downtime and zero data loss. Which DR strategy?

choices.why: Compute is off; not zero downtime.
Full capacity live in both regions.

cards.front: The database is continuously replicated to the DR region; EC2 is launched only during a disaster. Which strategy?

choices.why: Requires a scaled-down copy always running.

cards.front: You must centrally manage and automate backups of EBS, RDS, and DynamoDB across the organization. Which service?

back.explanation: One service with backup plans plus Vault Lock.

cards.front: You need cost-effective DR for 200 on-premises servers into AWS. Which service?

back.explanation: Continuous block replication; pay little until failover.

cards.front: You need a global relational database with a cross-region RPO of about 1 second. Which service?
You want users automatically routed to the standby region when the primary fails. What do you use?

back.answer: Route 53 failover routing with health checks

choices.text: Route 53 failover routing with health checks
choices.why: Failed health check flips DNS to DR.
